correctness.rationale: Independent all-n check: filter the oriented-incidence complex by the number of left arrows. With none, the join of the n two-choice right-arrow complexes is an (n−1)-sphere. Adding one left arrow attaches a cone along a cone: at its target just the opposite right arrow is available. Hence the subcomplex Y with at most one left arrow has the same equivariant homology as the join. The relative chains of (X,Y) split over ordered pairs A_i,B_j and are the augmented right-link chains shifted by two. For i=j the right link omits target i; for i≠j the target choices Y_i and X_j form one 0-sphere (both together make the forbidden four-cycle), joined with the n−2 remaining choices. Thus relative homology is n² lines, all in degree n. The boundary of a diagonal relative generator [A_i,B_i]*z (z the join cycle on remaining right vertices) maps, by using the two one-arrow cones, to (X_i−Y_i)*z up to sign, a generator of H_(n−1)(Y). This gives concentration and rank n²−1, including n=2. Without the left swap, f² relative lines are fixed, each with sign sgn(σ). With the swap, a fixed point of σ gives one diagonal line with sign (−1)^n sgn(σ), while a two-cycle fixes two off-diagonal lines with the opposite sign: the two left vertices and the paired target choices each reverse, the remaining n−2 right factors reverse, and the sign of the permutation of those factors is −sgn(σ). Subtract the single join line, of character (−1)^{ne} sgn(σ), to recover both formulas. The signed exterior-square, standard and unordered-pair traces give the stated rational module.
residual_risks: The attached finite tests were not re-executed and do not prove the arbitrary-n theorem. The independent filtration argument does not depend on retrieval of Jojić. The extra n=2 automorphisms are excluded by the statement.
